FOOTNOTES

1/ The appropriation made in this section is exempt from the provisions of section 35-190, Arizona Revised Statutes, relating to lapsing of appropriations. (FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote)

2/ A.R.S. § 37-1305 annually appropriates \$3,000,000 from the General Fund to the Fire Suppression Revolving Fund. Because this authorization is in permanent statute, \$3,000,000 of the appropriated amount is not included in the General Appropriations Act.

3/ The appropriation for the hazardous vegetation removal line item is exempt from the provisions of section 35-190, Arizona Revised Statutes, relating to lapsing of appropriations, through June 30, 2028. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

4/ The sum of \$1,000,000 is appropriated from the state General Fund in each of FY 2021, FY 2022, FY 2023, FY 2024, FY 2025, FY 2026, FY 2027, FY 2028, and FY 2029 to the Arizona Department of Forestry and Fire Management for deposit in the Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication Fund established by A.R.S. § 37-1309 to assist in preventing wildland fire and flooding. (FY 2020 General Appropriations Act footnote)

5/ The appropriation for the wildfire mitigation line item is exempt from the provisions of section 35-190, Arizona Revised Statutes, relating to lapsing of appropriations, until June 30, 2029. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

6/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$6,303,100 and 43 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Environmental County Grants

The Baseline includes \$250,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Environmental County Grants. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item have been used by Greenlee, Graham, Gila, Navajo, Cochise and Apache Counties for environmental projects that impact economic development in those counties. Previously funded projects included forest restoration, endangered species habitat protection, watershed restoration, and natural resource planning. DFFM must approve any project prior to expenditure of the monies.

Federal Debt Repayment

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Federal Debt Repayment. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

In the FY 2026 General Appropriations Act, the Legislature appropriated \$11,180,800 one-time from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund as an FY 2025 supplemental. The Legislature stipulated that the monies must be used to repay debts incurred to the federal government in the course of wildfire suppression activities and made the monies non-lapsing.

Fire Suppression

The Baseline includes \$3,200,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Fire Suppression. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item are used for fire suppression on state trust land and rural private land. A.R.S. § 37-1305 provides an annual appropriation of up to \$3,000,000 from the General Fund for fire suppression. Because this authorization is in permanent statute, only \$200,000 of the appropriated amount is included in the General Appropriations Act. (See Wildfire Mitigation line item for additional monies supporting fire suppression in Arizona.)

Hazardous Vegetation Removal

The Baseline includes \$3,039,300 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for a Hazardous Vegetation Removal program. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

This line item supports hazardous material removal programs that treat state and private lands through prescribed burning or thinning of flammable vegetation. This work can be conducted by DFFM crews or through fuel reduction grants to contractors.

Inmate Firefighting Crews

The Baseline includes \$902,700 and 13 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Inmate Firefighting Crews. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

These monies provide firefighting training for 12 inmate fire crews. The crews act as first responders and are used for fuel treatment and fire suppression.

Post-Release Firefighting Crews

The Baseline includes \$1,332,700 and 20 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Post-Release Firefighting Crews. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item provide firefighting training for recently released inmates who previously participated in Inmate Firefighting Crews (see Inmate Firefighting Crews line item). The Post-Release Firefighting Program allows program participants to work towards completing their wildland firefighting certification following release from Department of Corrections custody.

Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication

The Baseline includes \$1,000,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2020 General Appropriations Act appropriated \$1,000,000 from the General Fund to DFFM to deposit in the Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication Fund in each fiscal year of FY 2021 through FY 2029. Because these monies were advanced appropriated in the FY 2020 General Appropriations Act, these appropriations will not appear in subsequent General Appropriations Acts.

Monies in this line item are used to provide grants to other state agencies, cities, towns, counties, Indian tribes, and other political subdivisions and nonprofit organizations to fund projects that will assist in the prevention of wildfires and flooding and promote restoration of wildlife habitats by removing nonnative vegetation and replacing it with native vegetation. Saltcedar plants are an example of a nonnative vegetation species.

Northern Arizona Wildland Fire Training Facility

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a Northern Arizona Wildland Fire Training Facility. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(4,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund in FY 2027 for removal of one-time funding to establish a new wildfire suppression training facility near Flagstaff.

Monies in this line item fund the construction of a new operational base for the Flagstaff Fire Department's Wildfire Management Division and provide wildfire suppression training for local and regional firefighters. In addition to the \$4.0 million state-level appropriation in FY 2026, the City of Flagstaff has allocated \$650,000 to design the facility.

State Fire Marshal

The Baseline includes \$1,844,400 and 19.5 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the State Fire Marshal. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal enforces the state fire codes and provides training and education for fire personnel and the general public.

State Fire School

The Baseline includes \$291,700 and 1 FTE Position from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the State Fire School. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item primarily subsidize smaller rural volunteer fire departments attending Arizona State Fire School workshops which provide firefighting education. Besides \$200,000 for subsidizing these costs, the remaining \$91,700 and 1 FTE Position is used for liaison work with the Arizona State Fire Training Committee and other firefighter training activities.

US Forest Service Land Thinning

The Baseline includes \$1,703,400 and 17 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the US Forest Service Land Thinning line item. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item fund administrative costs for partnerships with the U.S. Forest Service to thin forests on federal land. DFFM anticipates clearing about 4,500 acres with this funding.

Wildfire Mitigation

The Baseline includes \$27,354,900 and 122 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Wildfire Mitigation line item. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item are to be used for personnel, operating costs, equipment, and contracted services to mitigate future fires. The Baseline would make the FY 2027 appropriation non-lapsing through June 30, 2029. In FY 2025, DFFM expended a total of \$16,413,200 from this line item as follows:

\$7,158,000 for 122 DFFM staff to oversee the work of 10 crews of 72 inmates working to remove hazardous vegetation.

\$832,300 for inmate crews and corrections staff.

\$3,888,100 for Department of Transportation program costs, general operating costs, and other equipment and maintenance.

\$2,486,600 for contracted personnel to support wildfire mitigation efforts.

\$2,048,200 for external project grants.

(See the Wildfire Mitigation section of the DFFM narrative in the FY 2023 Appropriations Report for more information on prior appropriations to this line item.)

Budget Stabilization Fund Use for Processing Wildland Fire Claims

Expenditures incurred by local districts are paid for by DFFM using monies from the BSF. DFFM then requests reimbursement from its cooperating federal partners. Federal reimbursements are provided to the State Treasurer to be deposited into the BSF.

A.R.S. § 35-144 authorizes DFFM to use up to \$20,000,000 in Budget Stabilization Fund (BSF) monies to pay wildland fire suppression claims.

DFFM coordinates the dispatch of local fire districts in response to wildland fires occurring on federal land.

As of October 20, 2025, DFFM reports using \$14,681,385 in BSF capacity for claims awaiting federal reimbursement. (See the Budget Stabilization Fund Use for Processing Wildland Fire Claims section of the DFFM narrative in the FY 2021 Appropriations Report for more information on DFFM's use of the BSF.)

Source of Revenue: Legislative appropriations, federal monies, interest, gifts, grants, donations, and any other monies received for the purpose of the fund. The fund may also receive revenues from the sale of long-term water augmentation bonds and from public-private partnership agreements.

Wildfire Mitigation

Purpose of Fund: To fund water supply development projects, including those that import water from outside of Arizona and other related expenses such as water studies, assessments, and environmental reviews. The FY 2026 budget appropriated \$30,000,000 as a FY 2025 supplemental for fire suppression, \$11,180,800 as an FY 2025 supplemental for federal debt repayment, and \$4,000,000 in FY 2026 to establish a wildfire suppression facility near Flagstaff.

Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication Fund (FFM2456/A.R.S. § 37-1309)

Source of Revenue: Legislative appropriations. The FY 2020 General Appropriation Act appropriated \$1,000,000 from the General Fund to the department in each of FY 2020 through FY 2029 to deposit into the Nonnative Vegetation Species Eradication Fund.

Purpose of Fund: To provide grants to other state agencies, cities, towns, counties, Indian tribes, other political subdivisions and nonprofit organizations for projects that will assist in fire and flood prevention, conservation of water, replacing nonnative vegetative species with native vegetative species and restoring native habitats. General Fund appropriation expenditures are not displayed to avoid double counting of appropriations.
